contracts/userInterfaces/IMorphoLoanSuba.content:
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity >=0.8.4 <0.9;

import {IComposeReceiverAccountBase} from "./IComposeReceiverAccountBase.sol";
import {ISubaccount} from "./ISubaccount.sol";

/*
 * What each action of the wire schema ({ILoanSubaccount}, where the payload layouts are) does on
 * this market.
 *
 * `ACTION_BORROW`. The account's whole idle FXRP balance - the authenticated bridged amount (the
 * codec's `amountLD`) plus any residue - becomes collateral, and the borrowed loan tokens go to
 * the payload's destination. The fee terms are the type's current terms at delivery (the front
 * end warns while a change is pending in the timelock and keeps deadlines short; see the spec).
 * It is a debt increase: pause-gated and subject to the per-type borrow switch, both of which
 * revert retriably. **The cover gate** applies to the post-borrow position: its collateral (the
 * supplied credit included), at the market oracle's price, must cover `1.155 / LLTV` of the new
 * debt plus twice the collectible fee - the same rule as the withdraw's, Morpho's own liquidation
 * line with a headroom, so it implies Morpho's health check - or the delivery reverts retriably
 * (`InsufficientRemainingCollateral`) with nothing supplied or disbursed. Morpho's check runs
 * first, inside its borrow, so a borrow past Morpho's own line (or under a dead oracle) fails
 * there with Morpho's error instead; and unlike the withdraw, a borrow has no oracle-free route -
 * it needs the oracle back.
 *
 * `ACTION_WITHDRAW`. **The exit gate**: the withdrawal passes while the collateral remaining
 * after it, valued at the market oracle's price, covers `1.155 / LLTV` of the live debt plus
 * twice the collectible fee (1.5x at the launch market's 77% LLTV - Morpho's own liquidation line
 * with a headroom, so the gate implies Morpho's health check), and otherwise reverts retriably
 * (`InsufficientRemainingCollateral`, carrying the required cover and the remaining value) - debt
 * and fee are paid in loan tokens through {repay}, never taken from the collateral, so no price
 * ever moves funds here. Every failure leaves the delivery retriable, and this is the one place
 * what recovers it is written out. A quote shortfall: retry the SAME packet with more value.
 * Another transient return-send failure: retry the same packet once its cause clears - more value
 * cannot help, since exactly the newly quoted fee is forwarded. An uncovered remainder
 * (`InsufficientRemainingCollateral`, which a dead or zero-priced oracle also produces, since
 * it values the remainder at nothing): repay - send loan tokens to the account and let {repay}
 * split them pro rata between debt and fee (every payment shrinks the required cover; covering
 * both settles the position once the fee has actually been collected - a fee the collector
 * cannot receive stays owed and reserved, and a later {repay} retries it) - after which the
 * retried delivery passes, oracle-free once nothing is owed; or sign a smaller withdrawal. Bad
 * `returnOptions` frozen into the signed packet (the accepted residual - no retry can fix the
 * blob itself): issue a corrected instruction reusing the SAME operation id, whereupon the parked
 * packet later duplicate-skips. Position health is enforced by Morpho.
 *
 * `ACTION_DEPOSIT_COLLATERAL`. Supplies the account's whole idle FXRP balance as collateral on
 * its one market: the authenticated bridged amount (the codec's `amountLD`, which must be
 * non-zero) plus any residue waiting for the permissionless rail, less whatever that rail already
 * put into the position before delivery; no debt changes hands. While the controller is paused it
 * executes only when the position carries live debt (the defensive case - protecting an
 * endangered position); a debt-free deposit is new exposure and waits out the pause. With a
 * principal it checkpoints the fee first, as {depositIdleFxrp} does.
 *
 * `ACTION_CANCEL`. Consumes the id and nothing more: no market read, no fee terms, no borrow
 * switch, no collateral or debt moves. It is not pause-gated, since revoking an authority is not
 * new exposure.
 */

/**
 * @title IMorphoLoanSubaccountRemote
 * @notice User interface for the loan-chain-side subaccount (Ethereum, at launch), at the same
 * CREATE2 address as its Flare counterpart. Authenticated compose payloads, sent by this same
 * account on Flare, execute the typed actions on the type's write-once Morpho market — so the
 * address itself commits to the pool. Repayment, idle-collateral deposit and the fee
 * checkpoint are permissionless fixed rails, and nothing here is parent-callable. Idle FXRP
 * has one route, into the position ({depositIdleFxrp}), from where
 * the signed withdraw action brings it home under the position's ordinary conditions. Across
 * the rails and the signed actions every destination is fixed on-chain - the account's own
 * position, the parent, the governance-set fee recipient, or (the withdraw's return leg) this
 * account's own address on Flare - while the one user-chosen destination is a signed
 * borrow's disbursement. It has no native rail.
 */
interface IMorphoLoanSubaccountRemote is IComposeReceiverAccountBase, ISubaccount {

    /**
     * @notice The position as the front end needs it, projected to the current block: Morpho's
     * debt brought forward the way its accrual will bring it (the market's rate model over the
     * time since the market's last update), the fee's current period priced at the snapshotted
     * terms. Every field is a quote for the observed block - the contract recomputes at delivery.
     * @param collateral Collateral in the Morpho position, in collateral-token base units.
     * @param idleCollateral Collateral on the account, not in the position: the deposit rail, the
     * deposit action or the next borrow supplies it; a withdrawal leaves it where it is, so it is
     * not withdrawable position collateral.
     * @param idleLoanToken Loan tokens on the account: repay fuel, a reserved fee or a retained
     * surplus, all of which the next {repay} consumes.
     * @param debt The live Morpho debt, interest to this block included.
     * @param feeDebtX18 The fee payable now - the running period projected to this block - at
     * WAD precision (base units x 1e18); the whole units, `feeDebtX18 / 1e18`, are the
     * collectible.
     * @param oraclePrice The market oracle's price (1e36 scale); zero when the oracle is dead
     * or answers zero - the gate then values the collateral at nothing.
     * @param collateralValue `collateral` at that price, in loan tokens.
     * @param lltv The market's liquidation LTV (WAD).
     * @param requiredCover The cover gate's demand on the position as it stands, in loan tokens.
     * @param morphoHealthFactor Morpho's distance to liquidation, `collateralValue x lltv / debt`
     * (WAD): above 1e18 healthy, 1e18 on Morpho's line; the maximum value when debt-free; zero
     * when the oracle is dead with live debt. Flare's cover is the stricter line - compare
     * `collateralValue` with `requiredCover` for that one.
     * @param liquidationPrice The lowest oracle price (1e36 scale) at which Morpho still holds
     * the position healthy, both of its floor steps included: one unit below it the position is
     * liquidatable. Zero when debt-free (never liquidatable), the maximum value when there is
     * debt and no collateral (liquidatable at any price).
     */
    struct LoanPosition {
        uint256 collateral;
        uint256 idleCollateral;
        uint256 idleLoanToken;
        uint256 debt;
        uint256 feeDebtX18;
        uint256 oraclePrice;
        uint256 collateralValue;
        uint256 lltv;
        uint256 requiredCover;
        uint256 morphoHealthFactor;
        uint256 liquidationPrice;
    }

    /**
     * @notice What the cover gate and the market allow next, projected to the current block.
     * @param maxBorrowByCover The largest further borrow the cover gate passes once the idle
     * collateral and `additionalCollateral` are supplied with it (Morpho's own rounding
     * included); zero under a dead oracle. The cover check only: the pool's liquidity
     * (`marketLiquidity`), the pause, the borrow switch and the transport are separate
     * conditions.
     * @param marketLiquidity The loan tokens the pool can still lend: its supply total minus its
     * borrow total, both brought to this block. Morpho refuses a borrow above it.
     * @param maxWithdraw The largest withdrawal the cover gate passes on the position as it
     * stands: the whole collateral when nothing is owed, zero under a dead oracle otherwise. The
     * cover check only; the pause and the transport are separate conditions.
     */
    struct LoanLimits {
        uint256 maxBorrowByCover;
        uint256 marketLiquidity;
        uint256 maxWithdraw;
    }

    /**
     * @notice What a {repay} would do now with the loan tokens already on the account plus a
     * top-up - the EXPECTED allocation: a fee transfer the collector's token refuses is deferred
     * or reserved at execution instead, so the fee then stays owed and the debt takes its share.
     * Oracle-free, like {repay} itself. The payment allocated is the loan tokens on the account
     * plus the top-up.
     * @param feePaid The fee collected: the pro-rata share of a payment short of debt plus fee,
     * the whole collectible otherwise.
     * @param debtPaid The Morpho repayment.
     * @param surplus Pushed to the parent - only once the debt is closed; anything else that is
     * left stays on the account (a reserved fee, or the remainder of a partial payment).
     * @param debtAfter The Morpho debt afterwards, Morpho's rounding included.
     * @param collectibleAfter The fee still payable afterwards.
     * @param closingTopUp The top-up that closes both claims now: debt plus collectible, less
     * what is already on the account.
     */
    struct RepayPreview {
        uint256 feePaid;
        uint256 debtPaid;
        uint256 surplus;
        uint256 debtAfter;
        uint256 collectibleAfter;
        uint256 closingTopUp;
    }

    /**
     * @notice Whether a withdrawal of a given amount passes the cover gate now, and what
     * reopens it if not. The cover check only: an amount above the collateral, the pause and the
     * transport are Morpho's and the delivery's own refusals.
     * @param coverSatisfied True when the cover check passes the withdrawal on the position as
     * it stands - the check, not a promise of execution.
     * @param requiredCover The cover the gate demands, in loan tokens.
     * @param remainingValue The collateral left after the withdrawal at the oracle's price;
     * zero under a dead oracle.
     * @param minimumTopUp The smallest loan-token top-up whose {repay}, together with the loan
     * tokens already on the account, makes the withdrawal pass - the expected allocation, see
     * {previewRepay}; zero when it already passes. Closing both claims always suffices.
     */
    struct WithdrawPreview {
        bool coverSatisfied;
        uint256 requiredCover;
        uint256 remainingValue;
        uint256 minimumTopUp;
    }

    /**
     * @notice Whether a borrow of a given amount, with the idle collateral and a packet's
     * collateral supplied first, passes the cover gate now - the cover check only; the pool's
     * liquidity is reported beside it, the pause, the borrow switch and the transport are
     * separate conditions, and the amount is not otherwise validated.
     * @param coverSatisfied True when the post-borrow position passes the cover check.
     * @param requiredCover The cover the gate demands of the post-borrow position, in loan
     * tokens.
     * @param collateralValue The supplied collateral - in the position, idle and the packet's -
     * at the oracle's price; zero under a dead oracle.
     * @param debtAfter The Morpho debt after the borrow, its share rounding included.
     * @param marketLiquidity The loan tokens the pool can still lend; Morpho refuses a borrow
     * above it.
     */
    struct BorrowPreview {
        bool coverSatisfied;
        uint256 requiredCover;
        uint256 collateralValue;
        uint256 debtAfter;
        uint256 marketLiquidity;
    }

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a borrow action executes.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param operationId The user-chosen operation id, now consumed.
     * @param collateralSupplied FXRP supplied in this execution: the whole idle balance - the
     * bridged credit plus any residue, less whatever the permissionless deposit rail had already
     * put into the position (zero for a message-only borrow with nothing idle).
     * @param borrowAmount Loan-token amount borrowed and disbursed (non-zero).
     * @param destinationKind The destination kind (see the `DESTINATION_KIND_*` constants).
     * @param destination The disbursement destination.
     * @param guid The LayerZero message id the action arrived with.
     */
    event LoanOpened(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        bytes32 operationId,
        uint256 collateralSupplied,
        uint256 borrowAmount,
        uint8 destinationKind,
        bytes32 destination,
        bytes32 guid
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a deposit-collateral action executes.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param amount FXRP supplied in this execution: the whole idle balance - the bridged credit
     * plus any residue, less whatever the permissionless deposit rail had already put into the
     * position.
     * @param guid The LayerZero message id the action arrived with.
     */
    event CollateralDeposited(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 amount,
        bytes32 guid
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a withdraw action executes; the withdrawn collateral is bridged
     * home in the same execution ({FXrpBridgedToOrigin} follows).
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param operationId The user-chosen operation id, now consumed.
     * @param amount Collateral withdrawn from the position and bridged.
     * @param guid The LayerZero message id the action arrived with.
     */
    event CollateralWithdrawn(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        bytes32 operationId,
        uint256 amount,
        bytes32 guid
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a cancel action consumes an operation id, so the borrow or withdraw
     * packet carrying that id can no longer execute. Absent when the id was already consumed -
     * the original won the race, or the cancellation was delivered twice.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param operationId The operation id now consumed.
     * @param guid The LayerZero message id the cancellation arrived with.
     */
    event LoanActionCancelled(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        bytes32 operationId,
        bytes32 guid
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when idle loan tokens are repaid into the account's position.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param assets The assets repaid (clamped to the live debt).
     */
    event LoanRepaid(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 assets
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when idle FXRP is deposited as collateral into the account's position.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param amount The amount deposited.
     */
    event IdleFxrpDeposited(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 amount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when FXRP is bridged back to this account's address on the origin
     * chain, to be redeemed on arrival: a withdraw action's return leg.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param amount The amount bridged.
     * @param originEid The origin chain's LayerZero endpoint id.
     * @param guid The LayerZero message id of the bridge-back send.
     */
    event FXrpBridgedToOrigin(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 amount,
        uint32 originEid,
        bytes32 guid
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when native value is forwarded to the parent Personal Account
     * (the remote implementation): the excess of a withdraw action's return-leg fee, or the whole value of a
     * terminally skipped withdraw delivery - it must not strand on an account with no
     * native rail.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address paid.
     * @param amount The native value forwarded.
     */
    event NativeSweptToParent(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 amount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted after each fee checkpoint and re-baseline, degenerate ones included
     * (zero principal or a zero elapsed period skip the fee math but still re-baseline).
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param principal The canonical Morpho debt measured at the checkpoint (base units); a
     * borrow or repayment in the same call re-syncs it afterward
     * ({LoanFeePrincipalSynced}), and {getLoanFeeState} is authoritative.
     * @param feeDeltaX18 The fee accrued for the interval (base units at WAD precision); zero
     * on degenerate checkpoints.
     */
    event LoanFeeCheckpointed(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 principal,
        uint256 feeDeltaX18
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a borrow or repayment re-syncs the fee base to the canonical
     * post-action debt (the clock and terms snapshot stay).
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param principal The canonical Morpho debt after the action (base units) - the base
     * the next period is priced on.
     */
    event LoanFeePrincipalSynced(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 principal
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when accrued fee is paid to the fee recipient in loan tokens: from the
     * account's balance in {repay} (the fee's pro-rata share of a partial payment, or, once
     * the debt is closed, as much of the collectible as the balance covers).
     * @param feeRecipient The collector paid.
     * @param amount The amount paid (whole base units; the fee debt shrinks by exactly this).
     */
    event LoanFeeCollected(
        address indexed feeRecipient,
        uint256 amount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a sub-unit fee remainder is forgiven at an exit gate: on a
     * debt-free position it can never be
     * transferred (ERC-20 moves whole base units) and never grows again, so a raw-zero gate
     * would park the exit forever over less than one base unit. Never more than a sub-unit
     * remainder: a whole base unit or more stays owed.
     * @param remainderX18 The forgiven remainder (base units at WAD precision, below 1e18).
     */
    event LoanFeeRemainderForgiven(
        uint256 remainderX18
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted with the amount of outstanding fee covered by loan tokens retained on
     * the account instead of leaving as surplus; a later {repay} retries from it. A snapshot,
     * not a delta: repeated calls can emit the same amount, and a collection that empties the
     * balance reserves zero (the claim then lives only in the fee debt).
     * @param feeRecipient The collector the reservation is owed to.
     * @param amount The reserved amount (whole base units).
     */
    event LoanFeeReserved(
        address indexed feeRecipient,
        uint256 amount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when the initial pro-rata attempt of a partial {repay} failed to pay
     * the fee's share - the token refused the recipient (RLUSD can freeze addresses). The share
     * stays in the repayment balance and repays debt; if that closes the debt, the remainder
     * is attempted again and whatever still cannot be paid is reserved on the account
     * ({LoanFeeReserved}). Whatever the call leaves unpaid stays owed; a later {repay}
     * collects it.
     * @param feeRecipient The collector the share was owed to.
     * @param amount The unpaid share (whole base units).
     */
    event LoanFeeDeferred(
        address indexed feeRecipient,
        uint256 amount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a closed position's loan-token surplus is sent to the parent
     * Personal Account (the user's own account on this chain) at the end of {repay}.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address paid.
     * @param amount The surplus amount.
     */
    event LoanSurplusRecovered(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 amount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a closed position's loan-token surplus could not be sent to the
     * parent Personal Account (the token refused the transfer - RLUSD can freeze addresses)
     * and stays on the account. The repayment itself stands; a later {repay} retries the push.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address that refused.
     * @param amount The surplus amount retained.
     */
    event LoanSurplusRetained(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 amount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when an authenticated action completes without executing. The bridged
     * FXRP that arrived with the message stays on the account, recoverable along the fixed
     * rails.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param operationId The payload's operation id. A duplicate was already consumed; an
     * expired skip leaves it unconsumed (the intent can retry under it).
     * @param reason The skip reason (see the `SKIP_REASON_*` constants).
     * @param guid The LayerZero message id the action arrived with.
     */
    event LoanActionSkipped(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        bytes32 operationId,
        uint8 reason,
        bytes32 guid
    );

    /**
     * @notice Reverts on a debt increase while new borrowing is disabled for this account's
     * subaccount type — the routine way a pool is sunset. Deliberately a revert, not a skip:
     * the condition is temporary-by-policy and a permissionless delivery must not consume
     * the packet.
     */
    error BorrowingDisabled();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts a debt increase before the subaccount type's fee recipient activates
     * its terms: a registered-but-unpriced type cannot take on debt. Retriable - the packet
     * is not consumed by this temporary condition.
     */
    error FeeTermsNotConfigured();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if there are no idle loan tokens.
     */
    error NothingToRepay();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if there is no idle FXRP to deposit.
     */
    error NothingToDeposit();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if the OFT's live peer for the origin chain no longer matches the pinned
     * one; the return leg fails closed instead of bridging toward an unknown remote OApp.
     */
    error WrongOriginPeer();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if the delivered compose value does not cover the return leg's LayerZero
     * messaging fee.
     * @param required The required fee.
     */
    error InsufficientFundsForBridgeHome(
        uint256 required
    );

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if excess or skipped compose value could not be forwarded to the parent
     * (this account has no native exit); the delivery stays retriable.
     */
    error RefundFailed();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts a withdraw delivered below its signed compose-value floor, so that an
     * underfunded permissionless delivery cannot consume the packet - not even as a terminal
     * skip. Retriable.
     * @param required The signed delivery-value floor.
     */
    error InsufficientDeliveryValue(
        uint256 required
    );

    /**
     * @notice Reverts a withdraw or borrow action that would leave the position uncovered: the
     * collateral remaining after it, at the market oracle's price, would be worth less than
     * `1.155 / LLTV` of the live debt plus twice the collectible fee (a dead or zero-priced
     * oracle values it at nothing). Retriable: repay - loan tokens to the account and {repay} -
     * or sign a smaller withdrawal or borrow, then retry.
     * @param requiredCover The collateral value the gate demands, in loan tokens.
     * @param remainingValue The value the action would have left, in loan tokens; zero under
     * a dead or zero-priced oracle.
     */
    error InsufficientRemainingCollateral(
        uint256 requiredCover,
        uint256 remainingValue
    );

    /**
     * @notice Reverts on a borrow with an unsupported destination kind (the Wormhole-to-XRPL
     * kind is reserved but not implemented).
     * @param destinationKind The unsupported destination kind.
     */
    error UnsupportedDestinationKind(
        uint8 destinationKind
    );

    /**
     * @notice Reverts on a borrow that names a delivery-value floor for a destination kind that
     * spends no compose value on this chain. Every kind V1 supports disburses without spending
     * value, so the floor must be zero; the field is reserved in the frozen payload for a kind
     * that pays for its own onward delivery. The Flare sender refuses the same instruction
     * before any bridge fee is paid.
     */
    error UnexpectedDeliveryValueFloor();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts on a borrow disbursement destination that is not a clean zero-padded
     * EVM address, or is zero or this account.
     */
    error InvalidDestination();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts on an action carrying no amount: a borrow with a zero borrow amount, a
     * deposit with no bridged amount, or a withdraw of zero.
     */
    error ZeroAmount();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if a withdraw's signed arrival floor for the return leg is not one the
     * withdrawal can honor: zero, or above the amount being withdrawn.
     * @param amount The amount being withdrawn and bridged home.
     * @param minAmountReceived The floor the instruction signed.
     */
    error InvalidMinAmountReceived(
        uint256 amount,
        uint256 minAmountReceived
    );

    /**
     * @notice Repays the account's debt and the accrued Flare fee with its idle loan-token
     * balance: a payment short of the two is split pro rata between them, a covering one
     * closes the debt, attempts the whole collectible (reserving anything unpaid) and returns
     * the surplus to the parent.
     * @dev Permissionless and pause-exempt throughout: the debt reduction only moves the
     * account's own position toward safety, and the fee legs only move money to Flare's own
     * recipient. It checkpoints before the repayment and re-syncs
     * the canonical debt after (see {checkpointFee}). With live debt `D` and collectible fee
     * `F`, interest accrues, then a balance `P < D + F` pays `P × F / (D + F)` (rounded down)
     * to the fee recipient first and repays Morpho with the rest - by exact borrow shares when
     * that rest covers the debt (no over-repay revert), otherwise by assets; a balance covering
     * `D + F` closes the debt by exact shares and attempts the whole collectible from the
     * remainder. Every fee payment is best-effort, never held by the pause (an overcharge
     * would land on Flare's own recipient and is refundable), never rolling back the
     * repayment ({LoanFeeCollected}; the fee debt shrinks only by the
     * successfully requested transfer, conventional ERC-20 semantics being a
     * market-registration policy): a share that cannot be paid stays in the balance and
     * repays debt ({LoanFeeDeferred}), and once debt-free the remainder is attempted again,
     * with as much of it as the outstanding fee needs reserved here ({LoanFeeReserved}). Only
     * the unreserved balance is pushed to the parent once debt-free ({LoanSurplusRecovered};
     * best-effort, {LoanSurplusRetained} on refusal). Settling both claims through this rail
     * therefore costs the live debt plus the collectible fee, from one balance in one call; a
     * payment that covers the debt but not the fee leaves a pro-rata sliver of both, unless
     * the debt closes for less: a paid share's round-down can leave exactly the debt (possible
     * within roughly `F / D` base units of `D + F`), and a deferred share leaves the full
     * payment available, which may cover it - Morpho then consumes exactly the debt and the
     * tail handles any remainder, with fee still outstanding. The default route pays the fee
     * alongside the debt; repaying Morpho directly, on this account's behalf, pays the debt
     * alone.
     * @return _assets The assets repaid.
     */
    function repay()
        external
        returns (uint256 _assets);

    /**
     * @notice Runs a bare fee checkpoint: prices the elapsed period at the snapshotted
     * terms, adds the result to the fee debt, and re-baselines (principal to the canonical
     * live debt, clock to now, snapshot to the current terms).
     * @dev Permissionless and pause-exempt - notably the liquidated account's relief: an
     * external repayment or liquidation lowers the debt without the account seeing it, so the
     * floor keeps accruing on the stale principal until someone checkpoints, and only
     * prospectively; a liquidation's interest is still estimated from the recorded shares.
     * Under unchanged terms and non-decreasing debt, splitting a period typically increases
     * the total fee and never decreases it by more than one X18 unit (under 1e-18 of a base
     * unit) per checkpoint, so checkpointing cannot be used against the protocol; the
     * advertised promise is that per-checkpoint measurement. Shares-first: zero principal
     * makes no Morpho call, zero live shares read Morpho's stored totals without touching the IRM.
     */
    function checkpointFee()
        external;

    /**
     * @notice Deposits the whole idle FXRP balance as collateral into the account's position.
     * @dev Permissionless with a fixed destination (the account's own position): the retry
     * rail for FXRP that arrived without a successful composed action. It remains available
     * while paused only to defend a position with live debt; a debt-free deposit is new
     * exposure and is pause-gated. With a principal it checkpoints the fee first, and when that
     * has to accrue (live shares, time elapsed) Morpho's accrual must succeed, as for {repay};
     * the fee itself is never paid or gated here.
     * @return _amount The amount deposited.
     */
    function depositIdleFxrp()
        external
        returns (uint256 _amount);

    /**
     * @notice Returns the account's fee state, as of the last checkpoint or post-action
     * sync (stored values, not a live projection - run {checkpointFee} first for current
     * numbers).
     * @return _principal The canonical Morpho debt at the last checkpoint or sync (base
     * units).
     * @return _feeDebtX18 The accrued, uncollected fee at WAD precision (base units × 1e18);
     * the fractional part below one base unit is carried, never discarded.
     * @return _collectible The fee payable now: `_feeDebtX18 / 1e18`, whole base units.
     * @return _lastCheckpoint The last checkpoint's timestamp.
     * @return _feeFloor The snapshotted floor the next elapsed period is priced at (WAD).
     * @return _feeSpread The snapshotted spread the next elapsed period is priced at (WAD).
     */
    function getLoanFeeState()
        external view
        returns (
            uint256 _principal,
            uint256 _feeDebtX18,
            uint256 _collectible,
            uint64 _lastCheckpoint,
            uint64 _feeFloor,
            uint64 _feeSpread
        );

    /**
     * @notice The position projected to the current block - see {LoanPosition}. Reverts with the
     * market's rate model when it does, and where canonical accrual would overflow (a dead IRM
     * blocks every debt-bearing action anyway); a dead oracle is reported, not thrown.
     */
    function getLoanPosition()
        external view
        returns (LoanPosition memory);

    /**
     * @notice The cover gate's and the pool's bounds on the next borrow and withdrawal - see
     * {LoanLimits}.
     * @param _additionalCollateral Collateral a borrow packet would bring, counted as supplied.
     */
    function getLoanLimits(
        uint256 _additionalCollateral
    )
        external view
        returns (LoanLimits memory);

    /**
     * @notice The expected outcome of a {repay} over the loan tokens on the account plus
     * `_additionalLoanToken` - see {RepayPreview}. Oracle-free, and shares-first like {repay}: a
     * debt-free account's preview reads no rate model either.
     * @param _additionalLoanToken The top-up to preview; zero previews the idle balance alone.
     */
    function previewRepay(
        uint256 _additionalLoanToken
    )
        external view
        returns (RepayPreview memory);

    /**
     * @notice Whether a withdrawal of `_amount` passes the cover gate now, and the smallest
     * top-up whose {repay} would make it pass - see {WithdrawPreview}.
     * @param _amount The collateral to withdraw, in collateral-token base units.
     */
    function previewWithdraw(
        uint256 _amount
    )
        external view
        returns (WithdrawPreview memory);

    /**
     * @notice Whether a borrow of `_amount` passes the cover gate now, once the idle collateral
     * and `_additionalCollateral` are supplied - see {BorrowPreview}.
     * @param _amount The loan tokens to borrow.
     * @param _additionalCollateral Collateral the borrow packet would bring, counted as supplied.
     */
    function previewBorrow(
        uint256 _amount,
        uint256 _additionalCollateral
    )
        external view
        returns (BorrowPreview memory);
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity >=0.8.4 <0.9;

import {ISubaccount} from "./ISubaccount.sol";

/**
 * @title IRedeemingSubaccount
 * @notice The surface every Flare subaccount type whose idle FXRP means one thing - home -
 * shares: the permissionless rail `sweepRedeem`, which pushes the whole balance to the parent
 * Personal Account and has it redeemed to the XRPL owner. Home is the only public direction on
 * such an account. Every entry a type gives the redemption pays the same price - the
 * controller's executor fee - and redeems the same balance; what becomes of a balance FAssets
 * will not redeem is the parent's decision ({IPersonalAccount.redeemFromSubaccount}).
 */
interface IRedeemingSubaccount is ISubaccount {

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when idle FXRP is pushed to the parent Personal Account and redeemed by
     * it to its XRPL owner.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address (the redeemer).
     * @param amount Amount of FXRP pushed and requested for redemption (the whole balance,
     * from whichever entry).
     * @param redeemedAmount Amount of FXRP actually redeemed, which can be less; the rest
     * stays on the parent, or came back here when it is itself redeemable, for the next sweep.
     */
    event FXrpRedeemed(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 amount,
        uint256 redeemedAmount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when a redemption pushed a balance FAssets will not redeem - below its
     * minimum - to the parent Personal Account, which kept it unredeemed (in place of
     * {FXrpRedeemed}).
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param token The FXRP token.
     * @param amount The pushed amount.
     */
    event TokenSweptToParent(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        address indexed token,
        uint256 amount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Emitted when the value a redemption carried stayed with the parent Personal
     * Account instead of being spent as the executor fee: nothing was redeemed, so the parent
     * kept it.
     * @param parentPersonalAccount The parent Personal Account address.
     * @param amount The amount sent.
     */
    event NativeSweptToParent(
        address indexed parentPersonalAccount,
        uint256 amount
    );

    /**
     * @notice Reverts on an empty account: a redeem-home packet whose credit a sweep already
     * moved stays retriable, and a caller's value is returned rather than trapped.
     */
    error NothingToRedeem();

    /**
     * @notice Reverts if the value a redemption carries - `msg.value` on {sweepRedeem}, the
     * compose value on a type's authenticated entry - is below the controller's executor fee.
     * @param executorFee The required value.
     */
    error InsufficientFundsForRedeem(
        uint256 executorFee
    );

    /**
     * @notice Redeems all idle FXRP through the parent Personal Account, to its XRPL owner.
     * @dev Permissionless and parameterless: the destination is the parent (fixed at
     * deployment, part of this account's address), which pulls exactly the pushed amount and
     * requests its redemption through {IPersonalAccount-redeemFromSubaccount} - never more, so
     * its own balance stays out of it - so every outcome - a partial fill when FAssets tickets
     * run out, a payment-default payout, a refund - remains under the user's control.
     * `msg.value` must reach the controller's configured executor fee
     * ({InsufficientFundsForRedeem}; the price of the permissionless rail, and of every other
     * entry to the same redemption) and travels whole as the FAssets executor fee (recorded in
     * whole gwei). The whole balance is redeemed rather than whole lots; an empty account
     * reverts ({NothingToRedeem}). A balance below the FAssets minimum the parent keeps
     * unredeemed, with the value ({TokenSweptToParent} and {NativeSweptToParent} in place of
     * {FXrpRedeemed}, `_redeemedAmount` zero); an unfilled remainder of a partial fill comes
     * back here when it is itself redeemable, and stays on the parent otherwise.
     * @return _amount The balance the sweep saw (the whole balance).
     * @return _redeemedAmount Amount of FXRP actually redeemed; zero when FAssets redeemed none.
     */
    function sweepRedeem()
        external payable
        returns (uint256 _amount, uint256 _redeemedAmount);
}

@title ComposeReceiverAccountBase contract
 @notice Shared authenticated `lzCompose` ingress and operation-id replay protection for the
 accounts that receive compose messages from their own twin on the other chain. Derived
 accounts define their action set ({_dispatch}), their transport source ({_getTransport}),

 parent-driven and public rails stay outside this base. The authentication is deliberately in
 one place: it is the security root of every action that arrives without a local signature.

documentation.text: @inheritdoc IMorphoLoanSubaccountRemote
@dev The subaccount's action set (see {ComposeReceiverAccountBase._dispatch}).

@dev The withdraw action spends compose value in the same call - the return leg's
 LayerZero fee, with the excess pushed to the parent - so it opts in; every
 other action must not carry value (a mistaken delivery stays retriable without it).
 @dev Adding `ACTION_BORROW` here is what enables a destination kind that pays for its own
 onward delivery, and it must account for the native in three places, not one: a
 SUCCESSFUL EVM disbursement would then be allowed to carry value it never spends (this
 path leaves native untouched, and the account has no rail to recover it, so that value
 must be refused or refunded), a terminal skip already sweeps to the parent, and whatever
 the onward delivery leaves unspent must go the same way.

@dev Consumes an operation id so the borrow or withdraw packet carrying it can never
 execute. Deliberately minimal: no pause check (revoking an authority is not new
 exposure), no deadline (a late cancellation is unnecessary or still correct), no market
 or terms read, nothing moved. An id already consumed - the original executed first, or
 this cancellation was delivered twice - finalizes without an event rather than
 reverting, so a lost race cannot leave the packet retriable forever.

typeDescriptions.typeString: function (uint256) view external returns (struct IMorphoLoanMarketsFacet.FeeTerms memory)

documentation.text:
@dev Supplies the whole idle FXRP balance as collateral - the authenticated bridged
 amount and any residue - without changing debt. The action carries no operation id and
 no deadline: a deposit only adds the user's own collateral, which the permissionless
 rail can do with the same tokens anyway, so a re-issued one (a new packet - a delivered
 compose cannot replay) deposits again and a late one
 is harmless (the same reasoning that leaves the Flare redeem-home id-less). During a
 pause only an indebted position may receive it - defending stays available, new
 exposure waits - and a temporary rejection reverts, leaving the packet retriable.

@dev Supplies the account's whole FXRP balance as collateral and returns the amount, zero
 when nothing is here. Every FXRP on this account is the user's own and has one route, the
 position: a packet's freshly delivered credit, a skipped packet's credit, a direct send -
 there is no distinction to draw, so all of it goes in. The permissionless rail may have
 put a credit into the position before its packet is delivered (the accepted race),
 leaving nothing to supply; a message-only borrow arrives with nothing idle by design.

@dev Borrows `_amount` on the position as it stands and sends it to the destination.
 The fee is checkpointed before and its principal re-synced after (an unsynced new
 principal would read as market interest at the next checkpoint), and the cover gate runs
 on the resulting position before anything leaves: a borrow past it reverts, retriably,
 with nothing sent. Morpho's own health check ran inside the borrow; the gate implies
 it, so it is the binding one whenever Morpho passed.

@dev The atomic withdrawal: withdraws collateral and bridges the withdrawn amount home
 with the redeem-home compose in the same execution - no idle window, so the redeposit race
 cannot touch a withdrawal. The delivered compose value pays the return leg's live quote
 against the signed `returnOptions`, with the excess to the parent; too little value or
 any other failure reverts and leaves the delivery retriable. Morpho enforces position
 health.

@dev The soft gates shared by the borrow and the withdraw - the deposit carries no id and no
 deadline (see {ComposeReceiverAccountBase._terminalSkipReason}):
 a duplicate id or a stale deadline completes the delivery without executing; the
 bridged FXRP stays for the fixed rails.

typeDescriptions.typeString: function (struct SendParam memory,bool) view external returns (struct MessagingFee memory)
function (struct SendParam memory,struct MessagingFee memory,address) payable external returns (struct MessagingReceipt memory,struct OFTReceipt memory)
function (struct SendParam memory,struct MessagingFee memory,address) payable external returns (struct MessagingReceipt memory,struct OFTReceipt memory)

documentation.text:
@dev The withdraw action's return leg: sends `_amount` FXRP to this account's
 own Flare address (same address on every chain) with the redeem-home compose - the
 action and nothing else - and the Flare twin redeems whatever it then holds, this
 arrival included, at the price of its own public rail. `_amount` is gross and
 `_minAmount` the floor the sender signed on what must arrive; equal validated decimals
 mean the two differ only by the fee-capable adapter's cut, and a cut above the allowance
 reverts the delivery (retriable) rather than taking it from the user's collateral.
 `_options` carry the Flare-side gas and, as compose value, the redemption's executor
 fee - at least the Flare controller's configured fee, or the redeem-home parks until a
 delivery brings it or anyone sweeps (the operator, for a packet a fee change caught in
 flight). Exactly the quoted fee is spent from `_value` and the excess is forwarded to the
 parent (the endpoint is no refund target).

typeDescriptions.typeString: function (uint256) view external returns (struct IMorphoLoanMarketsFacet.FeeTerms memory)

documentation.text:
@dev Prices the elapsed period at the SNAPSHOTTED terms - `owed = max(floor·P·T,
 I + spread·P·T)` with `I = max(0, D − P)` over the debt `D` the principal reached
 ({_debtReached}), so a repayment outside the rails lowers the interest observed while a
 liquidation keeps the interest the position bore - then re-baselines: principal, its
 shares and the collateral to the position now, clock to now, snapshot to the current
 terms. The re-baseline runs on EVERY checkpoint (a first borrow must accrue at current
 terms, not stale ones). Shares-first: zero principal makes no Morpho call; a zero elapsed
 period skips the fee math but still re-reads the position raw (a same-block checkpoint
 after an external repayment must not keep a stale base); zero live shares read the stored
 totals without accruing, so the IRM is never touched.

@dev The cover gate, shared by the withdraw (on the remainder after `_collateralOut`) and
 the borrow (on the post-borrow position, `_collateralOut == 0`): the collateral left in
 the position, valued at the market oracle's price, must cover {LoanMath.requiredCover} of
 the live debt and the collectible fee - Morpho's liquidation line with a fixed headroom, so
 the gate implies Morpho's health check and a fresh loan is gated at `EXIT_HEADROOM / LLTV`
 of its debt. The debt read here is accrued: the caller's checkpoint, or the borrow just
 made, brought it forward. With nothing owed the gate reads no oracle (and forgives
 debt-free dust); a zero, dead or reverting oracle values the remainder at nothing, so
 the action is refused - a withdrawal is then settled through repay, oracle-free, and
 retried, while a borrow needs the oracle back (Morpho, whose check ran first inside the
 borrow, reads it too). Reverts `InsufficientRemainingCollateral` with the two numbers.

@dev A sub-unit remainder on a debt-free position can never be transferred (ERC-20
 moves whole units) and never grows again - a raw-zero gate would park the exit
 forever over dust, so it is forgiven when a gate passes with nothing collectible.
 Reached only then, so the remainder is sub-unit by construction; a whole unit or more
 is a collectible fee and is never forgiven.

@dev Records the fee base from the position as Morpho stores it: the principal, the
 borrow shares behind it and the collateral ({_debtReached} compares against both).

@dev The tail of {repay}, over the balance a closed or debt-free position leaves: pay
 `min(collectible, balance)` to the fee recipient ({_payFee}, best-effort, never rolling
 back the repayment), then reserve as much of the still-outstanding fee as the remaining
 balance covers (a later repay retries that reservation without a new top-up; an
 uncovered shortfall needs new funds) and send only the unreserved balance to the
 parent, once debt-free.

@dev Pays `_amount` (non-zero) of the collectible fee from this account's balance to
 the fee recipient, best-effort: nothing moves when the token refuses the recipient
 (RLUSD can freeze addresses), so a repayment never rolls back; the fee debt shrinks
 only by the successfully requested transfer (conventional ERC-20 semantics are a
 registration policy). Not held by the pause: the money goes to Flare's own recipient,
 where an overcharge would be refundable, and holding it only made the paused route
 debt-first. Returns the amount paid - zero when nothing moved.

documentation.text:
@dev The account's one market, bound write-once to its type. If its Morpho stops
 answering, this account's debt-gated paths block - inherent to where the position
 lives; hence the operational policy of only canonical immutable Morpho Blue deployments
 of the pinned v1.0.0 implementation (any other needs the conformance verification repeated).
@dev The account's collateral on its market, a plain Morpho storage read.

@dev The account's live borrow shares on its market - the exact test for "is there
 any debt", read live from Morpho every time (nothing is cached).

@dev The pause rule shared by the two collateral deposits: defending an indebted position
 survives a pause, like repayment, while a debt-free deposit is new exposure and waits it
 out. Debt increases and withdrawals never route through here - they stop outright. The
 pause is read first, on every deposit: unpaused - the common case - that is one
 controller read and no position read, and a controller that cannot answer the pause
 question refuses every deposit, indebted or not, the same fail-closed posture as
 {_checkNotPaused}.
@dev The position and the market's borrow totals as Morpho stores them, without accruing.

@dev The debt the recorded principal reached, which the fee reads its interest from: the
 live debt, unless the position holds less collateral than expected - which, with every
 deposit and withdrawal tracked, only a liquidation causes. A liquidation burns shares, and
 with them interest the position bore; the recorded shares' value at the given totals keeps
 it. A repayment outside the rails leaves collateral in place and stays a donation, unless a
 liquidation falls in the same period, before or after it: the recorded shares are then
 credited whole, the repaid ones included.

@dev The market oracle's price, zero when the oracle is dead, reverting or answers zero -
 the gate's own treatment, so a quote reads the collateral the way the gate will.

typeDescriptions.typeString: function (struct IMorpho.MarketParams memory,struct IMorpho.Market memory) view external returns (uint256)

documentation.text:
@dev The market brought forward to this block the way Morpho's own accrual will bring it -
 the rate model's view rate compounded over the time since the market's last update, added
 to the borrow and supply totals within their uint128 bounds (a market without a rate model
 earns nothing) - and this account's shares, collateral and the debt those shares represent
 on the accrued totals. Reverts where the rate model does: every debt-bearing action would.

@dev The lowest oracle price at which Morpho's health check still passes: its value floors
 twice (the collateral's value, then that value at the LLTV), so the price is the smallest
 that keeps the floored value at or above `ceil(debt / LLTV)`. Zero when debt-free; the
 maximum value with debt and no collateral.

@dev The largest further borrow the cover passes against `_value` of collateral. The
 closed form - the claim the value covers, less the debt and the fee's weight - ignores
 Morpho's share rounding on the way in and out, so the exact bound is found by bisection on
 the post-borrow debt as {_borrowTo} will see it: zero passes (the position is
 covered, or the closed form would be zero) and two past the closed form fails (one beyond
 what a share of rounding can add; were it ever to pass, the result would be a passing,
 non-maximal amount, never an unsafe one).

@dev The debt after borrowing `_more` on the accrued market: Morpho rounds the new shares
 up on the way in and the debt up on the way out.

@dev {repay}'s allocation of `_payment`, assuming every fee transfer succeeds: with live
 shares, the pro-rata fee share first when the payment is short of debt plus fee, then the
 debt (closed by shares when the rest covers it, otherwise repaid by assets with Morpho's
 rounding), then the tail - the collectible from what is left, a reservation for the rest,
 the surplus to the parent only once debt-free.

@dev The smallest top-up whose {repay} (with `_idle` already on the account) leaves a
 position the cover passes at `_valueLeft`: a binary search over the top-up, since
 every unit paid shrinks both claims; closing both claims (debt plus collectible less the
 idle balance) always suffices, so the search is bounded.

@dev Whether the position {_simulateRepay} leaves after `_payment` is covered by

@dev The value, in loan tokens, of the collateral left after `_collateralOut` at `_price`,

@title MorphoLoanSubaccountRemote contract
 @notice The loan-chain-side subaccount implementation (Ethereum, at launch): same frozen
 proxy and CREATE2 address as the Flare-side account, resolved per type through the
 controller-as-beacon. Authenticated compose actions ({ComposeReceiverAccountBase}), sent by
 this same account on Flare, operate on its type's write-once Morpho market - so the address
 itself commits to the pool. Repayment, idle-collateral deposit and the fee checkpoint are
 permissionless fixed rails, and nothing here is parent-callable: Morpho collateral and debt
 move only behind the compose authentication. Idle FXRP has
 one route, into the position ({depositIdleFxrp}), from where the signed withdraw action
 brings it home under the position's ordinary conditions. Across the rails and the signed
 actions every destination is fixed on-chain - the account's own position, the parent, the
 governance-set fee recipient, or (the withdraw's return leg) this account's own address on
 Flare - so no caller ever
 chooses a destination, a market or an amount source. The one user-chosen destination is a
 signed borrow's disbursement, authorized by the XRPL signature its payload carries.
 @dev No native rail: the only protocol-delivered native is a withdraw delivery's compose
 value (the return leg's fee), spent or forwarded to the parent within the same call, so a
 plain send reverts; native landing without a call (pre-deployment funding, an LZ native
 drop, a force-send) strands until a beacon upgrade adds a rail - accepted.

documentation.text:
@notice Returns the borrow rate per second (WAD) of `marketParams`, updating the model's
 state; called by Morpho on accrual.

@notice Returns the borrow rate per second (WAD) of `marketParams` without updating the
 model's state.

@title IIrm
 @notice Minimal Morpho Blue interest rate model interface: the two rate entry points, as in
 the canonical `morpho-org/morpho-blue` `IIrm` v1.0.0. `borrowRateView` is what the account's
 read surface uses to bring a market's debt forward to the current block the way Morpho's own
 accrual will; `borrowRate` is the state-changing twin Morpho calls when it accrues. Kept as our
 own MIT code because the upstream files are GPL-2.0-or-later; conformance is pinned by
 `test/unit/smartAccounts/MorphoConformance.t.sol`.

@notice Accrues interest for a market, updating its totals.
 @param marketParams The market to accrue interest for.
@notice Returns the price of one collateral asset in loan-token assets, 1e36-scaled.
@dev WAD fixed point: the fee rates' and the headroom's precision.
@dev The fee's year: annual WAD rates accrue over a fixed 365-day year.

@dev The cover gate's headroom over Morpho's liquidation line (WAD): the collateral left
 after an action must be worth `EXIT_HEADROOM / LLTV` of the covered claim, where Morpho
 itself lets a position run down to `1 / LLTV` (its withdraw, borrow and liquidation tests
 are one and the same). At the launch market's 77% LLTV this is exactly 1.5x.

@dev The cover gate's required cover, in loan tokens: `(debt + FEE_WEIGHT * collectible)
 * EXIT_HEADROOM / lltv`, rounded up; zero when nothing is owed.

@dev The fee one elapsed period adds, at WAD precision (base units x 1e18):
 `max(P * floor * T / YEAR, I * WAD + P * spread * T / YEAR) - I * WAD` over the principal
 `P` at the period's start (base units), the WAD annual rates, the period's length `T` in
 seconds of the 365-day year, and the market interest `I = max(0, debtReached - P)` the
 period produced in base units, from the debt the principal reached - a debt that fell
 counts as zero interest, so the delta never underflows. Each rate term is one `mulDiv`
 rounded down, the interest exact. Zero for a zero principal or a zero period.

@dev The fee's share of a payment short of debt plus fee, `payment * collectible / (debt +
 collectible)` rounded down; the remainder goes to the debt.
@dev Morpho's market id for `_marketParams`.
@dev Shares for `_assets`, rounded up.
@dev Shares for `_assets`, rounded down.
@dev Assets for `_shares`, rounded up - what closing a borrow position costs.
@dev `_x * _y / 1e18`, rounded down (Morpho's `wMulDown`).

@title MorphoMath
 @notice Our own MIT implementation of the pieces of Morpho Blue arithmetic the accounts
 depend on: the market id (`keccak256(abi.encode(marketParams))`, Morpho's `MarketParamsLib.id`),
 the share/asset conversions with Morpho's virtual offsets (`SharesMathLib`: one virtual
 asset, 1e6 virtual shares, rounding as named) and the interest compounding of its accrual
 (`MathLib.wTaylorCompounded`, the third-order Taylor polynomial of `e^(rate * elapsed) - 1`
 that `_accrueInterest` applies to the borrow total). Written here rather than imported because the
 upstream libraries are GPL-2.0-or-later; equality with `morpho-blue` v1.0.0 (commit 55d2d99)
 is pinned by `test/unit/smartAccounts/MorphoConformance.t.sol` on fixed vectors. The full-precision `mulDiv`
 agrees with Morpho's checked multiplication everywhere Morpho itself does not revert.

@notice Reverts if the OFT's live peer for the destination chain no longer matches the
 peer pinned in the controller's bridge route for this subaccount's type.
@notice Reverts if the caller's excess native refund could not be returned.

@title IBridgingSubaccount
 @notice The surface every Flare subaccount type that bridges FXRP to its own address on a
 remote chain shares, whatever the type does there: the compose ingress of its own remote
 twin's messages (see {IComposeReceiverAccountBase}), authenticated against the transport
 derived from the type's bridge route, and the errors of the forward move every one of its
 instructions is sent through. The instructions themselves, and what an arriving message
 does, are declared on the type's interface (e.g. {ILoanSubaccount}); whether the type also
 redeems its idle FXRP is a separate surface ({IRedeemingSubaccount}).
@notice Reverts if `lzCompose` is called by anything other than the LayerZero endpoint.

@notice Reverts if native value is attached to `lzCompose` for an action that does not
 spend it within the same call. Rejecting it keeps a mistaken delivery retriable without
 value; an action that spends or forwards the value in the same call opts in (the Flare
 redeem-on-arrival, the loan-chain atomic withdraw).

@notice Reverts if the compose sender (`_from`) is not the configured FXRP OFT.
 @param from The compose sender.

@notice Reverts if the composed message did not originate on the configured origin chain.
 @param srcEid The source endpoint id of the message.

@notice Reverts on a payload with an unsupported schema version.
 @param version The unsupported version.

@notice Reverts on a payload with an unsupported action.
 @param action The unsupported action.
@notice Reverts on a payload whose operation id is zero.

@title IComposeReceiverAccountBase
 @notice The shared authenticated `lzCompose` surface of the same-address cross-chain
 accounts: the loan-chain subaccount and Personal Account (Ethereum, at launch), and the Flare
 loan subaccount as the receiver of its own bridge-back. It authenticates the endpoint, the
 OFT, the origin chain, the pinned peer and `composeFrom`, and tracks replay state for the
 signed actions (an id-less action, such as the Flare redeem-home - which itself originates
 from a signed withdraw - carries no id and relies on the endpoint's at-most-once
 compose delivery). Users are XRPL-only and their
 signatures become on-chain authority only on Flare, so every action arriving here was sent by
 this same address on the other chain — the account's own twin. Account-specific
 parent-driven and public rails live outside this interface.

@notice Reverts if the account is already initialized (including the implementation
 contract itself, which is locked in its constructor).
@notice Reverts if the controller address is invalid (zero).

@notice Returns the controller (MasterAccountController) address of this account.
 @return The controller address.

@notice The signed LayerZero options and delivery-value floor of the two-leg withdrawal.
 The operator quotes the return leg first, against `returnOptions` - so that quote already
 contains the redemption's executor fee those options buy - puts it (plus headroom; the
 excess lands on the parent) into `destinationOptions` as compose value, then quotes and
 sends the first message. One payment, made on Flare, covers both legs and the
 redemption.

@notice Reverts on a loan instruction whose arguments cannot execute on the loan chain:
 a zero operation id or a deadline already passed (borrow and withdraw), a zero borrow,
 deposit or withdrawal amount, a borrow disbursement that is not a clean non-zero EVM address other than
 this account, a borrow naming a delivery-value floor for a destination kind that cannot
 spend value, or a withdraw with a zero delivery-value floor. Checked here, before any
 bridge fee is paid.

@notice The borrow instruction: bridges `_collateralAmount` FXRP (zero for a borrow
 against existing collateral) with the typed payload that supplies it as collateral,
 borrows `_borrowAmount` on the loan-chain twin's market and disburses it. A pure
 collateral deposit is its own instruction, {depositCollateral}.
 @dev Restricted to the parent Personal Account: the instruction names a loan action and
 a user-chosen disbursement destination, so it must carry the user's XRPL signature. The
 payload is built here, not passed in, so a malformed payload cannot reach the bridge; the
 envelope and the EVM destination are validated before quoting
 ({InvalidLoanInstruction}) and the loan chain re-validates on delivery. It sends to this
 account's own cross-chain address through the configured pinned peer, sharing the
 bridging core's guards: paused reverts, a configured route that is not suspended required,
 live peer re-checked. `_extraOptions` must be type-3 options carrying both the destination
 `lzReceive` gas and the `lzCompose` gas. `msg.value` must cover the LayerZero fee; the
 excess is refunded to the parent. On the loan chain the borrow is also refused, retriably,
 when the post-borrow position would fall under the cover gate
 (`InsufficientRemainingCollateral`) - the same rule that gates {withdraw}: the collateral
 must be worth `1.155 / LLTV` of the debt plus twice the collectible Flare fee.
 @param _minCollateralAmount The least FXRP that must arrive on the loan chain; zero
 when `_collateralAmount` is zero, otherwise non-zero and at most that amount. The
 adapter is fee-capable, so this is the user's signed allowance for its cut - set it to
 `_collateralAmount` when no fee is expected.
 @param _collateralAmount FXRP to bridge and supply as collateral; may be zero, at most
 the account's balance.
 @param _borrowAmount Loan-token amount to borrow and disburse; non-zero.
 @param _destinationKind The disbursement destination kind (`DESTINATION_KIND_*`).
 @param _destination The disbursement destination (a clean zero-padded EVM address for
 `DESTINATION_KIND_EVM`).
 @param _minComposeValue The delivery-value floor for a destination kind that spends
 compose value on the loan chain, in the loan chain's native token. Reserved: every kind V1
 supports disburses without spending value, so `DESTINATION_KIND_EVM` requires zero and a
 non-zero floor is refused here, before any bridge fee. It exists in the frozen V1 payload
 to reduce what enabling a kind that does pay for its own onward delivery has to move -
 implementations and governed parameters rather than the wire schema. It does not
 guarantee that: a floor protects delivery funding and settles nothing about quote
 validity, a spending cap, or an XRPL destination tag, so a kind needing any of those
 still arrives as a new payload version. Its meaning, once such a kind
 exists, is the withdraw's: the loan chain refuses any delivery of this borrow - execution
 and terminal skip alike - carrying less than this, so a front-run with less cannot consume
 the packet and burn the prepaid value.
 @param _operationId The user-chosen operation id (non-zero, unique per subaccount).
 @param _deadline Unix time after which the loan chain skips the instruction unexecuted.
 Keep it short (under an hour): the loan is priced at the type's fee terms current at
 delivery, so the front end warns while a terms change is pending in the timelock, and a
 short deadline is what bounds how far past that warning a delayed packet can execute.
 @param _extraOptions Caller-supplied LayerZero execution options (type-3).

@notice The cancel instruction: a message-only send that consumes `_operationId` on the
 loan chain, so a borrow or withdraw packet carrying that id can never execute.
 @dev Restricted to the parent Personal Account. The motivating case is a borrow parked by
 a failed health check after a price drop, which any collateral landing - the user's own
 deposit or the permissionless rail - would otherwise make executable again. Sending this
 is not cancellation: the two packets race, an original that lands first executes
 normally and the cancellation then finalizes silently - so a client resolves a sent
 cancellation by whichever arrives, the loan chain's
 {IMorphoLoanSubaccountRemote.LoanActionCancelled} or the original action's own execution event,
 either of which ends the instruction's live state; and an id a cancellation was signed
 for is retired for good. It carries no deadline (a late
 cancellation is unnecessary or still correct). On the loan chain it is not pause-gated;
 here it travels the ordinary instruction path, which a Flare pause closes like every
 other instruction (the controller's instruction facets and the bridge send both check
 it), so a parked packet cannot be revoked from a paused Flare. In that state the loan
 chain's own pause suspends the borrow but cancels nothing, so the order is: pause the loan
 chain, restore Flare when safe, submit and confirm the cancellation while the loan chain
 stays paused, then resume - unpausing it earlier makes the latent packet executable again.
 Burning an unissued id is allowed and makes a re-send harmless.
 @param _operationId The operation id to consume; must be non-zero.
 @param _extraOptions LayerZero options for the cancel message (gas only - it moves no
 tokens and needs no compose value).

@title ILoanSubaccount
 @notice User interface for deterministic loan subaccounts on Flare: the parent-driven loan
 instructions, typed payload encoders over the shared forward move. The permissionless rail
 (`sweepRedeem`) is the redeeming surface every type whose idle FXRP means home shares, declared
 on {IRedeemingSubaccount}; the compose ingress of the loan-chain twin's messages is the bridging
 surface, declared on {IBridgingSubaccount}; the redeem-home action those messages carry
 ({ACTION_REDEEM_HOME}) is this type's own, dispatched into the same redemption as the rail.

@notice Reverts on a debt increase while new borrowing is disabled for this account's
 subaccount type — the routine way a pool is sunset. Deliberately a revert, not a skip:
 the condition is temporary-by-policy and a permissionless delivery must not consume
 the packet.
@notice Reverts if there are no idle loan tokens.
@notice Reverts if there is no idle FXRP to deposit.

@notice Reverts if the OFT's live peer for the origin chain no longer matches the pinned
 one; the return leg fails closed instead of bridging toward an unknown remote OApp.

@notice Reverts if excess or skipped compose value could not be forwarded to the parent
 (this account has no native exit); the delivery stays retriable.

@notice Reverts on a borrow that names a delivery-value floor for a destination kind that
 spends no compose value on this chain. Every kind V1 supports disburses without spending
 value, so the floor must be zero; the field is reserved in the frozen payload for a kind
 that pays for its own onward delivery. The Flare sender refuses the same instruction
 before any bridge fee is paid.

@notice Reverts on a borrow disbursement destination that is not a clean zero-padded
 EVM address, or is zero or this account.

@notice Reverts on an action carrying no amount: a borrow with a zero borrow amount, a
 deposit with no bridged amount, or a withdraw of zero.

@notice Repays the account's debt and the accrued Flare fee with its idle loan-token
 balance: a payment short of the two is split pro rata between them, a covering one
 closes the debt, attempts the whole collectible (reserving anything unpaid) and returns
 the surplus to the parent.
 @dev Permissionless and pause-exempt throughout: the debt reduction only moves the
 account's own position toward safety, and the fee legs only move money to Flare's own
 recipient. It checkpoints before the repayment and re-syncs
 the canonical debt after (see {checkpointFee}). With live debt `D` and collectible fee
 `F`, interest accrues, then a balance `P < D + F` pays `P × F / (D + F)` (rounded down)
 to the fee recipient first and repays Morpho with the rest - by exact borrow shares when
 that rest covers the debt (no over-repay revert), otherwise by assets; a balance covering
 `D + F` closes the debt by exact shares and attempts the whole collectible from the
 remainder. Every fee payment is best-effort, never held by the pause (an overcharge
 would land on Flare's own recipient and is refundable), never rolling back the
 repayment ({LoanFeeCollected}; the fee debt shrinks only by the
 successfully requested transfer, conventional ERC-20 semantics being a
 market-registration policy): a share that cannot be paid stays in the balance and
 repays debt ({LoanFeeDeferred}), and once debt-free the remainder is attempted again,
 with as much of it as the outstanding fee needs reserved here ({LoanFeeReserved}). Only
 the unreserved balance is pushed to the parent once debt-free ({LoanSurplusRecovered};
 best-effort, {LoanSurplusRetained} on refusal). Settling both claims through this rail
 therefore costs the live debt plus the collectible fee, from one balance in one call; a
 payment that covers the debt but not the fee leaves a pro-rata sliver of both, unless
 the debt closes for less: a paid share's round-down can leave exactly the debt (possible
 within roughly `F / D` base units of `D + F`), and a deferred share leaves the full
 payment available, which may cover it - Morpho then consumes exactly the debt and the
 tail handles any remainder, with fee still outstanding. The default route pays the fee
 alongside the debt; repaying Morpho directly, on this account's behalf, pays the debt
 alone.
 @return _assets The assets repaid.

@notice Runs a bare fee checkpoint: prices the elapsed period at the snapshotted
 terms, adds the result to the fee debt, and re-baselines (principal to the canonical
 live debt, clock to now, snapshot to the current terms).
 @dev Permissionless and pause-exempt - notably the liquidated account's relief: an
 external repayment or liquidation lowers the debt without the account seeing it, so the
 floor keeps accruing on the stale principal until someone checkpoints, and only
 prospectively; a liquidation's interest is still estimated from the recorded shares.
 Under unchanged terms and non-decreasing debt, splitting a period typically increases
 the total fee and never decreases it by more than one X18 unit (under 1e-18 of a base
 unit) per checkpoint, so checkpointing cannot be used against the protocol; the
 advertised promise is that per-checkpoint measurement. Shares-first: zero principal
 makes no Morpho call, zero live shares read Morpho's stored totals without touching the IRM.

@title IMorphoLoanSubaccountRemote
 @notice User interface for the loan-chain-side subaccount (Ethereum, at launch), at the same
 CREATE2 address as its Flare counterpart. Authenticated compose payloads, sent by this same
 account on Flare, execute the typed actions on the type's write-once Morpho market — so the
 address itself commits to the pool. Repayment, idle-collateral deposit and the fee
 checkpoint are permissionless fixed rails, and nothing here is parent-callable. Idle FXRP
 has one route, into the position ({depositIdleFxrp}), from where
 the signed withdraw action brings it home under the position's ordinary conditions. Across
 the rails and the signed actions every destination is fixed on-chain - the account's own
 position, the parent, the governance-set fee recipient, or (the withdraw's return leg) this
 account's own address on Flare - while the one user-chosen destination is a signed
 borrow's disbursement. It has no native rail.

@notice Reverts on an empty account: a redeem-home packet whose credit a sweep already
 moved stays retriable, and a caller's value is returned rather than trapped.

@notice Redeems all idle FXRP through the parent Personal Account, to its XRPL owner.
 @dev Permissionless and parameterless: the destination is the parent (fixed at
 deployment, part of this account's address), which pulls exactly the pushed amount and
 requests its redemption through {IPersonalAccount-redeemFromSubaccount} - never more, so
 its own balance stays out of it - so every outcome - a partial fill when FAssets tickets
 run out, a payment-default payout, a refund - remains under the user's control.
 `msg.value` must reach the controller's configured executor fee
 ({InsufficientFundsForRedeem}; the price of the permissionless rail, and of every other
 entry to the same redemption) and travels whole as the FAssets executor fee (recorded in
 whole gwei). The whole balance is redeemed rather than whole lots; an empty account
 reverts ({NothingToRedeem}). A balance below the FAssets minimum the parent keeps
 unredeemed, with the value ({TokenSweptToParent} and {NativeSweptToParent} in place of
 {FXrpRedeemed}, `_redeemedAmount` zero); an unfilled remainder of a partial fill comes
 back here when it is itself redeemable, and stays on the parent otherwise.
 @return _amount The balance the sweep saw (the whole balance).
 @return _redeemedAmount Amount of FXRP actually redeemed; zero when FAssets redeemed none.

@title IRedeemingSubaccount
 @notice The surface every Flare subaccount type whose idle FXRP means one thing - home -
 shares: the permissionless rail `sweepRedeem`, which pushes the whole balance to the parent
 Personal Account and has it redeemed to the XRPL owner. Home is the only public direction on
 such an account. Every entry a type gives the redemption pays the same price - the
 controller's executor fee - and redeems the same balance; what becomes of a balance FAssets
 will not redeem is the parent's decision ({IPersonalAccount.redeemFromSubaccount}).
@notice Reverts if the parent Personal Account address is invalid (zero).

@notice Returns the parent Personal Account address for this subaccount.
 @return The parent Personal Account address.

@notice Returns the subaccount type.
 @return The subaccount type.

@notice Returns the implementation address of the subaccount.
 @return The implementation address.

@title ISubaccount
 @notice The type-generic subaccount surface every implementation must expose. The frozen
 `SubaccountProxy` creation code embeds `initialize`'s exact selector and delegate-calls
 it from the proxy constructor, so a new subaccount type is not merely "any contract with a
 registered implementation": its implementation must implement this interface. Only the
 initializer's ABI is frozen with the proxy creation code — changing it shifts every predicted
 subaccount address; the rest of this interface is the protocol's requirement on every
 implementation, not something the proxy embeds.
@notice Emitted when the compose transport is cleared.

@notice Reverts if the LayerZero endpoint is not a contract, or is not the endpoint the

@title IComposeTransportFacet
 @notice The compose transport of a remote diamond: one record per diamond naming the
 LayerZero endpoint that may call `lzCompose`, the OFT that must be the compose sender, the
 origin chain and the pinned peer there. Every compose receiver on the diamond — the remote
 Personal Account and every remote subaccount type — authenticates against it, so it is the
 security root of every action that arrives without a local signature. One route per
 diamond: a token bridged through a different OFT would need a transport per route, which is
 a schema change, not a setting. Cut only on remote diamonds (the loan chain, Ethereum, at
 launch).
 @dev The transport is written under the timelock and cleared immediately: the clear is the
 containment lever for a compromised endpoint, OFT or peer, and a lever behind a timelock is
 not one. The clear does not cancel queued `setComposeTransport` calls (the timelock keys them
 by calldata hash and lets anyone execute a matured one - cancel them first), and it does not
 retire compose packets already queued at the endpoint (a delivery that reverts against a
 cleared transport stays retriable). The incident runbook is therefore: pause, cancel queued
 transport sets, clear, and later set a replacement transport that rotates the compromised
 identity - the exact compromised tuple is never restored, or packets forged under it would
 pass authentication again.

@dev The pool a subaccount type is bound to: a Morpho contract and a market on it.
 Write-once per type - positions live in it, so the binding must never change.

@dev A subaccount type's Flare fee terms: the user's effective rate is

 by the subaccounts. Set as one unit by timelock after registration, and changed the
 same way (accounts snapshot the terms they accrue under, so a change is never
 retroactive). Explicit zero rates are a deliberate "fee off".

 If n is a prime, then Z/nZ is a field. In that case all elements are inversible, except 0.
 If n is not a prime, then Z/nZ is not a field, and some elements might not be inversible.

@dev Variant of {invMod}. More efficient, but only works if `p` is known to be a prime greater than `2`.
 From https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermat%27s_little_theorem[Fermat's little theorem], we know that if p is
 prime, then `a**(p-1) ≡ 1 mod p`. As a consequence, we have `a * a**(p-2) ≡ 1 mod p`, which means that
 `a**(p-2)` is the modular multiplicative inverse of a in Fp.
 NOTE: this function does NOT check that `p` is a prime greater than `2`.

@dev Wrappers over Solidity's uintXX/intXX/bool casting operators with added overflow
 checks.
 Downcasting from uint256/int256 in Solidity does not revert on overflow. This can
 easily result in undesired exploitation or bugs, since developers usually
 assume that overflows raise errors. `SafeCast` restores this intuition by
 reverting the transaction when such an operation overflows.
 Using this library instead of the unchecked operations eliminates an entire
 class of bugs, so it's recommended to use it always.
